In nominal clauses S/A arguments take the ergative marker while the P argument is unmarked (accusative alignment). In relative clauses, when an A or P argument is relativized, the other core argument that remains inside the relative clause takes the ergative marker. When an oblique argument is relativized, the S/A argument inside the relative clause takes the ergative marker (accusative alignment).

There is a number-based split: the distinction between absolutive and ergative only occurs in the third person singular, while they are not marked in the dual and plural numbers. Another split occurs if the P argument "is backgrounded, is indefinite or only partly affected": P takes ablative case while the A argument takes absolutive case (forming an accusative alignment). This is considered an antipassivization by the source, but the verb does not take an antipassive marker in this context.
